transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Time: 15:00 UTC (48 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Porter (Redwood AE), Sam Khatri (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (NorthBay Head of ML), Daniel Ruiz (Platform Eng), Priya Anand (Security Lead)

Summary/Context: quarterly renewal check-in; NorthBay currently on Hosted API with a usage spike forecasted in Q4, wants EU region for latency + data residency and is evaluating Dedicated or Private VPC. Discuss contract extension terms (12 months preferred) and implementation timeline for EU region + pilot.

[00:00:05] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone — thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick agenda: renewal terms, eu region uplift, private/vpc questions, and timing for pilot. Maya, you wanted to lead with forecast?
[00:00:24] Maya (NorthBay): yeah thanks. so, Q4 we've got a product launch in ecom target europe — we're expecting about 3x token volume, and latency for EU users right now is not great. also compliance wants some level of data residency for logs and audit trails.
[00:00:38] Daniel: just to add, our infra team is nervous about burst patterns, we may need some reserved throughput rather than pure hosted.
[00:00:46] Alex: noted. Sam, can you quickly run through what options map to that?
[00:00:52] Sam (Redwood SE): sure — short answer: we can do Hosted with EU region enabled (fastest path), Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput), or Private (VPC / on‑prem) for full control. tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to spin up but shared tenancy; dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and lower p95 variability; private gives you full network control and KMS/HSM integrations but needs more lead time.
[00:01:20] Maya: for compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 1 year, SSO via our Okta, and SOC2 evidence. is that supported?
[00:01:30] Sam: yes — we have KMS integration for private and dedicated, and hosted supports envelope encryption with managed keys but if you need customer‑managed keys that's private/dedicated with KMS. SOC2 docs and our security pack are standard; we'll share the pack after this call.
[00:01:47] Priya (NorthBay): what's the difference in latency between hosted EU vs dedicated in eu? we want p95 < 220ms for short prompts.
[00:01:56] Sam: baseline hosted EU is usually around 180–240ms p95 depending on model and prompt size, dedicated can shave that to 140–190ms with co-located capacity and reserved batching. caveat: model choice and quantization also matter.
[00:02:12] Daniel: okay, and lead times? if we sign, how long until eu region is accepting traffic?
[00:02:18] Sam: for hosted EU, we can enable within 5–7 business days; dedicated requires provisioning GPU pools which is typically 3–5 weeks depending on capacity; private onprem/VPC pilot is 6–10 weeks for full rollout — that's an estimate.
[00:02:33] Alex: important to flag — NorthBay is also interested in a 12‑month extension in exchange for a discounted committed capacity. what's the rough ballpark discount for a 12‑month commitment on dedicated?
[00:02:44] Sam: ballpark across customers we've seen 15–25% depending on commit size. classic tradeoff: higher commit, deeper discount, and we can include burst allowances for seasonal spikes.
[00:02:56] Maya: we'd probably start with a modest commit and test the dedicated pool for the peak weeks. if we do that, can we set up canary routing back to hosted if dedicated has issues?
[00:03:05] Sam: yes — routing fallback is supported; you can specify policy to fail over to hosted or a lower‑cost model variant. we'll run through the routing rules in the pilot.
[00:03:18] Priya: security questions — audit trails, log retention; if eu data residency is required, do logs stay in eu?
[00:03:26] Sam: with EU VPC and private offering logs and metrics can be retained in the EU region and we can configure retention periods. hosted does store some telemetry in our central analytics; if that's a blocker, dedicated + VPC is recommended.
[00:03:40] Daniel: another question on KMS — we use AWS KMS with internal key rotations. how does Redwood handle key access and rotation?
[00:03:48] Sam: for dedicated/private we support customer‑managed keys (AWS KMS or HSM) and you maintain rotation policies; Redwood never has plaintext access to the keys. we'll provide the integration docs.
[00:03:59] Maya: great. timeline wise, we need EU region live before the marketing push on 2025-11-10. that's about eight weeks. is that feasible?
[00:04:07] Alex: eight weeks aligns with dedicated lead time if we move fast on procurement and the contract. hosted would be faster but won't meet the residency + KMS needs.
[00:04:16] Daniel: what about a hybrid approach? start hosted EU to validate user flows and then flip to dedicated/VPC for residency once committed? possible?
[00:04:24] Sam: absolutely — that's a common pattern. start hosted EU to get latency gains quickly, run the canary, then migrate route traffic to dedicated or private once provisioned. we can support session continuity and KV cache warmup strategies to reduce cold-start latency during the flip.
[00:04:44] Maya: regarding pricing — can you show a breakdown of per‑token, per‑embedding, and dedicated commit numbers? we want a simple comparison sheet to present to finance.
[00:04:53] Alex: yes, I'll send a side‑by‑side: Hosted EU incremental cost, Dedicated monthly committed pool pricing with discount tiers, and add‑ons like EU VPC, KMS integration, and extended log retention.
[00:05:04] Priya: we'll also want to run a security review with our auditors — can Redwood provide an SOC2 report and BAA?
[00:05:12] Jordan (CSM): we can share SOC2 v2 and our security packet; BAAs are handled via our legal team — we'll include details.
[00:05:19] Maya: ok, good. any blockers on our side besides procurement? we need details on provisioning steps and exact timelines so infra can plan maintenance windows.
[00:05:28] Sam: we'll provide a provisioning runbook that includes preflight checks, firewall rules, estimated lead times, and a step‑by‑step for migration.
[00:05:37] Daniel: also, token accounting — if we do dedicated commit, how do overages work if we exceed committed tokens in peak weeks?
[00:05:44] Sam: overages bill at a predetermined overage rate; we can also include burst capacity allowances that won't bill until a threshold. we'll outline options in the proposal.
[00:05:56] Alex: sounds like we have alignment on requirements. let's capture decisions: 1) Customer prefers 12‑month extension if committed discount is acceptable, 2) customer wants EU residency, KMS, and SOC2 deliverables, 3) plan a hybrid start with Hosted EU followed by Dedicated/VPC migration. does that capture it?
[00:06:15] Maya: yes that's accurate.
[00:06:18] Priya: yes
[00:06:20] Alex: ok next steps — I'll send proposal by Monday, Sam will send runbook and estimated lead times, Jordan will set pilot planning. anything else?
[00:06:29] Maya: one small thing — can you include a short note on model variants and quantization recommendations for cost savings? we plan to use a mid‑sized model for checkout and a larger one for high‑value sessions.
[00:06:38] Sam: sure; we'll include profiling suggestions — quantization, sequence length bucketing, and batching configurations.
[00:06:45] Daniel: last question — procurement asks if there are any early termination penalties for the committed plan?
[00:06:51] Alex: standard early termination applies; we can discuss a phased scale schedule and make it flexible for first 90 days with a rollback clause — I can propose language.
[00:07:01] Priya: thanks.
[00:07:03] Alex: great — we'll follow up. thanks everyone.

(TRANSCRIPT NOTES: occasional overlaps, filler words, and some names/transcription artifacts as typical. references: proposal template link: https://redwood.company/proposals/northbay-q425 (placeholder), security pack: https://redwood.company/security-pack (placeholder).)
recording_notes: Transcript includes natural crosstalk; some proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' rendered as 'keyv cache' in one snippet). Customer emphasized EU residency and KMS. Agreed hybrid runway: hosted->dedicated. See next steps and action items above.
